rows.grounds: present passive participle describing one undergoing cutting
optative expressing non-occurrence of being cut
compound indicating one who has reached that state
possessive compound indicating one whose mind is absorbed in that
comparative particle introducing the manner of invulnerability

items.question: Can a person absorbed in that state be harmed by physical cutting?
premises: A person may be physically subjected to cutting.
A person can be gone to that state.
A person can have the mind fixed on that state.
items.inference: One who has reached that state and whose mind is fixed on it is not truly cut even while being cut.
uncertainties: The referent of 'that' depends on the preceding verses and is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Just as one who has gone to that and whose mind is fixed on that, though being cut, is not cut.
